latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Target doubling FY25 revenue by FY28; EBITDA margin of 12-15%; positive free cash flow; zero overdue payments; 1-2 tech acquisitions; 1.0-1.25% revenue invested in R&D; fair dividends; zero deviation in EHS/compliance.
outlook.title: Guidance / outlook

outlook.body: All-time high backlog; international order from Egypt (Apr 2026); 765kV disconnector orders commercialized (Jan 2026)
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Expansion into Vietnam, Malaysia, Bangladesh, Africa, Middle East; global exhibitions in Kenya, Rwanda, Ethiopia, Tanzania; potential tech acquisitions; digital twin and AI in design/engineering; UK market penetration
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Build a broader engineering business with clearer priorities, greater operating discipline, and the capability to participate across multiple growth segments, per the Group's three-year strategic roadmap begun in FY26.
- Diversify across Transmission & Distribution (SSPSE), Protection & Control (Acrastyle) and Industrial Automation (HART) to widen opportunity and reduce concentration risk, while exploring operating synergies across the three businesses.
- Acrastyle: expand Design and Build engineering-led project capability beyond the established Build to Print business, and bring all engineering activities in-house to reduce order backlog and improve lead times.
- HART: expand into compatible spares and service-oriented, OPEX-based engagements to create a more balanced revenue mix and reduce dependence on CAPEX-led customer investment cycles; pursue a longer-term 'HART 2030 and Beyond' plan covering technology leadership, market expansion and leadership succession.
- SSPSE: scale output and profitability, and develop the 765 kV disconnector opportunity (FY27 priorities; further geographic-expansion detail in the source text is truncated).
- Group-wide investment in technology (product development, R&D, IPR), manufacturing capacity, quality/EHS/compliance systems, SAP and centralised reporting, and leadership development to strengthen execution and prepare each business for future scale.
outlook.title: Strategy

outlook.body: The Group increased manufacturing capacity in the UK (Acrastyle) by 40% during FY26 through redevelopment of the Ulverston facility (modernised buildings, improved operational layouts), with further expansion planned at Kolkata and Chennai. Acrastyle's manufacturing capacity expansion was recently completed per the Chairman's letter. SSPSE advanced its high-voltage disconnector portfolio with development of a new 765 kV class disconnector, completing type testing including at KEMA in Prague during the year.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global investment in electrification continues, driven by renewable energy integration and upgrades to electrical networks.
- The aluminium sector is seeing increased investment around consumption, efficiency and sustainability, benefiting HART's addressable market.
- Investment in the UK electricity network is increasing, driven by electrification, renewable energy integration and the transition towards Net Zero, supporting Acrastyle's opportunity.
- Acrastyle's order intake moderated following the conclusion of the TS2 investment programme and longer lead times from its opening order backlog.
- SSPSE's renewed export focus translated into orders across Bangladesh, Nepal and African grid modernisation projects; closer engagement with EPC customers is building relationships intended to support repeat business and wider market access.
- Material costs have risen and supply chains remain stretched, making it harder to add capacity and capability quickly.
- Acrastyle's FY26 revenue growth reflected converting order momentum built over recent years into revenue, with a backlog from a record FY25 order intake affecting lead times during FY26.
- SSPSE began FY26 with a record order book and focused on converting this into higher output, better execution and broader market presence.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: S&S Power is transforming from a legacy switchgear manufacturer into a technology-led global player in high-voltage disconnectors and industrial automation, leveraging strategic capex, export growth, and proprietary systems like REDCon to capture high-margin niches in aluminum and energy sectors. With FY26 revenue up 43% and EBITDA margins expanding, it's on track to double revenue by FY28 while targeting 12-15% EBITDA and debt-free status.

open.item: Acrastyle expects revenue to grow by approximately 20% in FY27, supported by conversion of the existing order book and continued investment in people, facilities and operational capabilities.
Group roadmap for FY2028 targets improving EBITDA margins to 12-15%, generating positive free cash flow and expanding in select export markets, while doubling organic revenue over the 2025 base.
Group ambition to grow organic revenue by around 25% annually, subject to market conditions, thereby doubling the business on a rolling three-year basis, while growing EBITDA by 33%.

Acrastyle's manufacturing capacity expansion was recently completed per the Chairman's letter. SSPSE advanced its high-voltage disconnector portfolio with development of a new 765 kV class disconnector, completing type testing including at KEMA in Prague during the year.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- technology: In-house engineered core technologies for aluminium process automation — evidence: HART 'engineers its own core technologies in-house and pairs them with deep application knowledge to deliver intelligent automation solutions for aluminium process applications'
- distribution: Established Protection and Control Panel Framework Agreements with six of the UK's seven electricity distribution companies and serves two of the three UK transmission operators — evidence: Acrastyle MD letter states these framework agreements and operator relationships
- scale: Acrastyle has more than 25,000 units deployed worldwide since 1995 — evidence: 'more than 25,000 units deployed worldwide'

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Execution risk on capex and international expansion; currency/foreign regulatory exposure; supply chain delays; competition from global players; reliance on aluminum industry demand; technology adoption pace

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: HART’s REDCon system for aluminum smelters is a proprietary, high-margin niche with limited global competition; Acrastyle’s UK presence provides regulatory credibility and export gateway to EU/UK markets

strategy.title: Strategy
strategy.body:
- Build a broader engineering business with clearer priorities, greater operating discipline, and the capability to participate across multiple growth segments, per the Group's three-year strategic roadmap begun in FY26.
- Diversify across Transmission & Distribution (SSPSE), Protection & Control (Acrastyle) and Industrial Automation (HART) to widen opportunity and reduce concentration risk, while exploring operating synergies across the three businesses.
- Acrastyle: expand Design and Build engineering-led project capability beyond the established Build to Print business, and bring all engineering activities in-house to reduce order backlog and improve lead times.
- HART: expand into compatible spares and service-oriented, OPEX-based engagements to create a more balanced revenue mix and reduce dependence on CAPEX-led customer investment cycles; pursue a longer-term 'HART 2030 and Beyond' plan covering technology leadership, market expansion and leadership succession.
- SSPSE: scale output and profitability, and develop the 765 kV disconnector opportunity (FY27 priorities; further geographic-expansion detail in the source text is truncated).
- Group-wide investment in technology (product development, R&D, IPR), manufacturing capacity, quality/EHS/compliance systems, SAP and centralised reporting, and leadership development to strengthen execution and prepare each business for future scale.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] HART (Hamilton Research & Technology) acquired in 2024, adding customized hardware/software solutions for aluminum plants worldwide.
- [Management] New management team inducted starting Feb 2024, including MD & Group CEO Krishnakumar Ramanathan (ex-Siemens) and new CEOs for each subsidiary.
- [IPR] Target to create 1-2 strong IPRs per company per year.

one-line thesis: S&S Power is transforming from a legacy switchgear manufacturer into a technology-led global player in high-voltage disconnectors and industrial automation, leveraging strategic capex, export growth, and proprietary systems like REDCon to capture high-margin niches in aluminum and energy sectors. With FY26 revenue up 43% and EBITDA margins expanding, it's on track to double revenue by FY28 while targeting 12-15% EBITDA and debt-free status.
guidance / outlook: Target doubling FY25 revenue by FY28; EBITDA margin of 12-15%; positive free cash flow; zero overdue payments; 1-2 tech acquisitions; 1.0-1.25% revenue invested in R&D; fair dividends; zero deviation in EHS/compliance.
order book & pipeline: All-time high backlog; international order from Egypt (Apr 2026); 765kV disconnector orders commercialized (Jan 2026)
segment / subsidiary detail: SSPSE: 36kV-765kV disconnectors, retrofits, spares; Acrastyle: protection & control panels for aluminum smelters; HART: customized hardware/software for aluminum plants, including POT controllers and FIRECon systems
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into Vietnam, Malaysia, Bangladesh, Africa, Middle East; global exhibitions in Kenya, Rwanda, Ethiopia, Tanzania; potential tech acquisitions; digital twin and AI in design/engineering; UK market penetration
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin improved to 4.8% in FY26 (from 2.7% in FY25); cost optimization via lean manufacturing, streamlined PM/CM/SCM, and zero overdue payments driving margin expansion
capex / expansion: Comprehensive capex plan underway: 765kV commercialization, LVCC scale-up, WMS development, factory expansion, SAP implementation, solar panels, cybersecurity, and digital twin R&D
capital allocation: 1.0-1.25% of revenue to R&D; ESOPs for talent retention; proportional annual dividends; capex for capacity and tech; zero debt accumulation target by Mar 2028
risks & watch-items: Execution risk on capex and international expansion; currency/foreign regulatory exposure; supply chain delays; competition from global players; reliance on aluminum industry demand; technology adoption pace
non-obvious takeaways: HART’s REDCon system for aluminum smelters is a proprietary, high-margin niche with limited global competition; Acrastyle’s UK presence provides regulatory credibility and export gateway to EU/UK markets

themes.title: Power transmission & renewable-evacuation capex
themes.need: Grid build-out to evacuate ~90 GW of new renewables is the broadest theme in the universe - pulling EHV/765kV transmission EPC, towers, conductors, OPGW, cables and HVDC. POWERGRID/ADANIENSOL TBCB pipeline plus state RDSS/underground-cabling capex (Rajesh Power 544291, OMPOWER) underpins multi-year visibility for EPC, tower (KP Green 544150, SKIPPER) and conductor/cable makers (KEI, RRKABEL, DYCL).
themes.driver: Fresh TBCB awards + execution ramp; EPC order inflows over next 1-2 quarters.

hero.oneLiner: A Chennai-based transmission & distribution equipment group operating across three businesses — switchgear/disconnectors (SSPSE), UK-based Protection & Control panels (Acrastyle), and industrial automation for aluminium smelters (HART).
